tripwires: a band is an integer run of z5 (0.2 deg) cells: z5 cells are whole by construction, z9 cells may split across two adjacent bands and are merged with associative aggregates (first only under a per-group constancy contract); exactness does not depend on edge alignment, it depends on membership arithmetic being exact integers on the declared lattice (round(lat / base) // cells_per_z5), never IEEE division of the latitude -- Polars evaluates col / 0.2 differently on a 1-row frame than in bulk
z0 is derived from the z5 rung in banded mode, never from the base
key_columns_by_tier default None must leave every existing lane byte-identical (pin with a digest test)
NoData is a class row (evt_code -9999), not a per-row count: a per-row count summed over class rows double-counts

one how per column across all rungs; a per-rung how is not a platform concept

part bounds handed to the derivation must come from the writer's receipts in the same call, never from a store-global memo: another process re-exporting the day leaves a stale memo that retracts every rung as derived-empty

banded base tables must carry 4326 cell ORIGINS (k * base), never centroids: round(lat / base) is unambiguous only on the lattice, and a centroid in a one-row part records a z5 range the bulk filter excludes; write_banded_base_day refuses non-origin rows

band membership and the derive floor agree exactly on lattice origins (snapped floor_to_resolution + origins guard); a z9 or z5 cell split across two bands is a regression, asserted zero across the envelope in test_banded_derivation.py; _merge_split_cells is retained as defence in depth, not a live path
